business_problem: Bumble's on-premises warehouse could not scale with growing reporting demand, causing collisions between ETL and ad hoc queries, rising licensing costs, and too much operational effort to maintain separate data tools.
solution_summary: Bumble standardized its reporting estate on Snowflake to replace an on-premises warehouse that could not keep ETL, analytics, and user concurrency from colliding as the company grew. Data warehouses, BI workloads, and raw data-lake storage now run on one Snowflake platform with full SQL support and cheaper long-term retention for raw data. Analysts, software engineers, and business users all work from the same governed base instead of moving between separate tools, while collaboration features let the data infrastructure team evaluate and integrate new products without copying data. Because compute and storage scale independently, users can run ad hoc queries without interrupting reporting or ETL, and the team can preserve unprocessed data longer for new use cases. The result is a single source of truth across about 15 internal products, lower maintenance overhead, and a platform that can keep scaling without the compromises Bumble faced on premises.

Business users, analysts, and engineers then query the same governed platform for BI, reporting, ETL, and exploratory analysis without disrupting one another's workloads.
business_outcome: Bumble created one source of truth for roughly 15 internal products, scaled to hundreds of users without query collisions, retained raw data longer for new use cases, and reduced the engineering effort previously spent managing on-premises hardware and complex workarounds.
